_readme: Round 7 of 7 (final) — big august 9th batch (in-copyright PDFs). Synopses grounded in real detect.mjs-extracted text; mentions curated from candidates.json per docs/detector.md exclusion rules; genres per tools/genres.mjs. Three PDFs across the whole batch could not be processed (no extractable text, and no PDF rendering tool available in this sandbox to fall back on): Atomic Habits (James Clear), The Algebra of Infinite Justice (Arundhati Roy), and the-pathans.pdf (unidentified — filename has no title/author, likely a scanned image PDF).

books.title: White Fragility: Why It's So Hard for White People to Talk About Racism
books.author: Robin DiAngelo
books.synopsis: DiAngelo argues that most white Americans are so racially insulated from discomfort about race that even mild challenges to that comfort—like being called out for a racist remark—trigger a defensive reaction she calls white fragility, and she traces how this dynamic protects the racial status quo. Drawing on decades of running diversity trainings, she dissects moves like color-blindness and color-celebration claims that let white people position themselves as exempt from racism.

books.title: Words Are My Matter
books.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
books.synopsis: A collection of talks, essays, introductions, and book reviews (mostly from 2000-2016) in which Le Guin discusses genre, fantasy, science fiction, gender, aging, and the craft of writing, and reviews and introduces the work of writers including H. G. Wells, José Saramago, Italo Calvino, and Margaret Atwood.

books.title: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
books.author: Robert M. Pirsig
books.synopsis: A narrator and his son Chris ride a motorcycle from Minnesota toward the West Coast with friends, alternating road observations and practical talk about motorcycle repair with the narrator's recovered memories of his former self, Phaedrus, a philosophy teacher whose obsessive pursuit of a definition of Quality led him through Kant, Aristotle, and Poincare toward a breakdown and electroshock treatment.

books.title: Zodiac: An Eco-Thriller
books.author: Neal Stephenson
books.synopsis: Boston-based rogue environmental activist and industrial chemist Sangamon Taylor tracks toxic dumping by corporations like Basco, using sewer outfalls, illegal sampling, and stunts staged from a Zodiac inflatable boat, before uncovering a genetically engineered organism plot tied to Basco executive Alvin Pleshy. The story climaxes in a violent confrontation on Boston Harbor with Pleshy and Biotronics president Laughlin, leaving Sangamon's friend Boone badly wounded.

books.title: Atmosphere: A Love Story
books.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
books.synopsis: Joan Goodwin, a physics teacher turned NASA astronaut candidate in the early 1980s, trains alongside fellow astronauts Vanessa Ford, Griff, Lydia Danes, and Hank Redmond in Houston while raising her young niece Frances, and falls in love with Vanessa; a present-day frame set on December 29, 1984 follows a shuttle mission in crisis after Griff and others are endangered during a spacewalk and reentry.

books.title: t zero
books.author: Italo Calvino
books.synopsis: A collection of speculative first-person monologues narrated largely by the cosmic being Qfwfq, ranging from the Moon's origin and the first birds to cellular mitosis and reproduction, and culminating in a story where the narrator becomes a character trapped in the Chateau d'If alongside Abbe Faria, watching Alexandre Dumas assemble the branching draft possibilities of the novel The Count of Monte Cristo.
